propositions: The original compact-on-close mechanism held the store write lock for up to 13m53s, starving concurrent agents, leaving no automatic compaction trigger and requiring manual rebar compact commands.

A two-arm selection mechanism must identify tickets for compaction: either small snapshot-less tickets with at least one foldable event (backfill), or already-snapshotted tickets whose foldable event count exceeds the threshold (recurrence).
Compaction must work in three environments: CI-driven by scheduled sweep (6-hourly), operation-linked by triggered fold after close, and nowhere else should the store lock be held by the fold itself.

Selection and folding must use the same predicate (is_foldable) and horizon (30-min default) so they cannot drift, and fold results must be counted honestly by observing *-SNAPSHOT.json artifacts before/after, not by return code.

An operation-linked floor must check cheaply after close whether the just-written ticket matches selection criteria or a last-sweep timestamp is stale, then spawn a detached compactor reusing enrich_drain's stamped advisory lock and PYTHONPATH bootstrap, with no foreground session wait.
